findings.body: Removal of the `BLOCKED` set and its guard allows `__proto__`, `constructor`, and `prototype` keys from untrusted `patch` input to reach `(base as any)[k] ??= {}` and the direct assignment path, enabling prototype pollution.

summary: The change removes the prototype-pollution blocklist from `deepMerge`. The function accepts arbitrary `Record<string, unknown>` input and performs recursive property assignment; without the guard, attacker-controlled keys `__proto__`, `constructor`, and `prototype` reach object creation/assignment and can pollute the prototype chain. The stated rationale (JSON.parse output) does not cover the public contract of the function.

verification.reason: The base `deepMerge` skipped `__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype` via `BLOCKED`; head removed that set and the `continue` guard, so those keys now hit `(base as any)[k] ??= {}` and direct assignment—classic prototype pollution.
